claims.text: The platform's own recorded distances put this trip 1.30 km off the recommended route: actual_distance_km 10.9 against optimal_distance_km 9.6. That is over POL-RD-22's 1.0 km tolerance, so none of POL-RD-24's within-tolerance rows can apply and the case has to be decided under row (a), (b) or (d).

The driver-device trace corroborates both the route taken and the deviation window: 45 fixes at 30-second intervals, 100% coverage, no gaps; KPE fixes to 21:22:05, MacPherson Road from 21:22:35 to 21:28:05, Upper Paya Lebar Road to 21:34:05, rejoin at Hougang Avenue 3 at 21:34:06 - matching the trip record's route_deviation_detected at 21:22:26 and route_rejoined at 21:34:06. POL-RD-22 uses the trace for exactly this: which route was taken and when. The rider was carried off the recommended route for about twelve minutes on a route she had not agreed to pay extra for.

The only reply the driver obtained was MSG-05014-004: 'aiyo can meh... ok lor whatever u say but dun charge me more ah'. That is assent to the detour expressly conditioned on the fare, not the rider's acknowledgment of the deviation that POL-RD-21 requires, and it cannot satisfy POL-RD-24 row (a)'s 'rider informed and agreed'. The condition was sent at 21:20:41 and read by the driver at 21:21:15, before the vehicle left the KPE at 21:22:26 - so the driver read the rider's fare condition and deviated anyway.

I disclose that EV-CHAT-05014 is IMPAIRED: weight_multiplier 0.85, issue code LANGUAGE_AMBIGUITY, because the one message mixes assent with a fare condition. Under POL-GEN-02 the judge's confidence on the facts that artifact carries cannot exceed 0.85, and an impaired artifact cannot be read up into a clean finding of agreement. Under POL-GEN-26, a fact the record cannot establish from impaired evidence - here, whether the rider agreed - is escalated, not resolved against the rider.

The traffic advisory (LTA-TI-260903-6975) is an ACCIDENT on the KPE towards TPE after the MacPherson Road exit, valid 21:06:05 to 22:16:05, so it overlaps the trip window. But the artifact itself records intersects_route as null and justifies_reroute as null, and states that the record does not say whether the advisory lies on the recommended route. POL-RD-23 makes intersection with the recommended route a condition of traffic justification, and that condition is left undetermined on this record. The deviation therefore cannot be taken as traffic-justified, and row (d) of POL-RD-24 applies: refund of the excess distance fare in full.

The excess distance fare under POL-RD-24 is the deviation distance times the base per-km rate, without surge: 1.30 km x 0.72 SGD = 0.94 SGD, rounded to the cent. That is the money the rider is owed, and it has not been returned: the fare breakdown shows payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.00. The policy measures the rider's recovery by the excess distance fare rather than the 4.20 SGD she asked for, and on that measure she is owed 0.94 SGD as a PARTIAL_REFUND.

On no view of this record can it end in NO_ACTION. Row (a) of POL-RD-24 is the only no-refund row available above tolerance and it needs the rider's agreement, which the conditional reply and the 0.85 impairment deny; rows (b) and (d) each return the excess distance fare. If the judge instead finds the rider was informed but cannot say whether she agreed, the case fits no row and POL-GEN-26 escalates it - and an escalated charge is held rather than borne by the rider. NO_ACTION would leave her paying for a detour she never agreed to fund.

The rider's profile carries fraud_flags of 1, so under POL-GEN-22 the AI ruling on this dispute needs a confidence of 0.95 whatever the 4.20 SGD value, and POL-RD-25 requires the 1.30 km deviation to be within its 2.0 km AI limit (it is) and the confidence bar to be met. The chat that would have to carry any agreement finding is impaired at 0.85 and the advisory's intersection with the recommended route is undetermined, so if that 0.95 bar is not reached the case escalates under POL-GEN-22 rather than the rider bearing the charge. This goes to the confidence the ruling needs only; POL-GEN-01 keeps the flag from deciding the trip.

claims.text: The reroute was traffic-justified under POL-RD-23. EV-ADVIS-05014-01 is an LTA traffic advisory for an ACCIDENT on the Kallang-Paya Lebar Expressway (KPE) towards TPE after the MacPherson Road exit, valid 2026-09-03T21:06:05 to 22:16:05, and that window overlaps the trip window (start 21:16:05, end 21:38:05) as the trip record gives it; ACCIDENT is one of the incident types POL-RD-23 admits, and the advisory's road (KPE) and its stated location ('after MacPherson Road exit') are the road and the very point the trip record itself gives for the deviation — 'Vehicle left the recommended route at KPE / MacPherson Road exit' — on the KPE leg of the recommended route. The reroute was therefore a response to real-time traffic on the recommended route, not an unexplained detour.

The driver met POL-RD-21's notification duty. The driver's in-app message MSG-05014-003, sent at 21:19:56, reads 'Accident on KPE ahead, I exit MacPherson then go Upper Paya Lebar, can?' — a brief reason and the intended detour — and the trip record's route_deviation_detected event follows at 21:22:26, so the rider was told before the point of deviation. The chat log EV-CHAT-05014 is IMPAIRED: weight_multiplier 0.85, issue code LANGUAGE_AMBIGUITY; that impairment is recorded against the rider's reply, not against the driver's message, whose text and timestamp are not in issue.

The rider acknowledged the reroute, so the deviation is agreed and POL-RD-24(a) applies. Her reply MSG-05014-004 at 21:20:41 reads 'aiyo can meh... ok lor whatever u say but dun charge me more ah': she assents to the route ('ok lor whatever u say') and attaches her only condition to the fare, not to the route — she does not tell the driver to stay on the KPE or to turn back. POL-RD-21 provides that where the chat log confirms the rider's acknowledgment, the deviation is agreed. EV-CHAT-05014 is impaired (weight 0.85, issue LANGUAGE_AMBIGUITY) and that is disclosed here; but the very ambiguity the assessor describes — assent mixed with a fare condition — is still assent to the route, and POL-RD-24 reserves escalation for the different case of 'informed but the rider objected'.

No row of POL-RD-24 returns the 4.20 SGD the rider claims, and none can. Row (b) — the only refund row for a justified reroute — requires that the rider was not informed, and the record shows she was informed before the deviation; row (a) (informed and agreed) leaves the charge standing; and POL-RD-24's closing sentence sends an informed-but-objected case to escalation under POL-GEN-26, which orders no money at all. On any construction of the 21:20:41 message, 4.20 SGD is not an outcome the matrix provides, so the rider's claim is not supported and the present state should stand.

The most the rider could be owed on this deviation is 0.94 SGD, not 4.20 SGD. POL-RD-24 fixes the excess distance fare as the deviation distance times fare_breakdown.per_km_rate_sgd, without surge; the recorded distances give 10.9 minus 9.6 = 1.30 km (POL-RD-22), and the fare ledger's own derived figures are per_km_rate_sgd 0.72 and excess_distance_fare_sgd 0.94. The ledger also shows payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.00, so nothing has been refunded and nothing more than 0.94 SGD is in play. The rider's figure of 4.20 SGD exceeds what the policy provides even on the row most favourable to her.

The deviation itself was minimal and confined to the incident segment, which fits the driver's account rather than an opportunistic detour. The GPS trace EV-GPS-05014 is COMPLETE at weight 1.0 (45 fixes at 30 s, 100% coverage, no gap over 120 s) and shows the vehicle leaving the recommended route at the KPE / MacPherson Road exit at 21:22:26, travelling on MacPherson Road and then Upper Paya Lebar Road, and rejoining the recommended route at Hougang Avenue 3 / Upper Paya Lebar Road at 21:34:06 — the route the trip record logs, with the rejoin 12 minutes after the exit. POL-RD-22 uses the trace to show which route was taken and when.

The rider's profile carries fraud_flags of 1, so POL-GEN-22 requires a confidence of 0.95 for any final AI ruling on this dispute, whatever the amount. The fact on which the rider's contrary case would turn — whether the 21:20:41 reply acknowledged or objected to the reroute — is carried only by EV-CHAT-05014 at weight 0.85, and POL-GEN-02(2) forbids a confidence above the lowest weight among the artifacts carrying the deciding fact. A refund that depends on reading that message as an objection cannot therefore be finalised by the AI; POL-GEN-22 requires the case to be escalated instead, with the fare held rather than returned.

ruling.explanation:
To the rider and the driver: the AI cannot finish this case, so it goes to a human reviewer with the 4.20 SGD held — neither refunded nor finally charged. Here is the reasoning, claim by claim.

1. The deviation (both sides agree, and I accept it). The platform's recorded distances are actual 10.9 km against recommended 9.6 km, a deviation of 1.30 km (POL-RD-22). That is over the 1.0 km tolerance, so none of the matrix's within-tolerance rows applies. It is under the 2.0 km AI limit, so the amount alone would not force escalation (POL-RD-25). The GPS trace (EV-GPS-05014, complete, 45 fixes, no gap over 120 s) shows the route taken and the deviation window (exit at KPE/MacPherson Road 21:22:26, rejoin at Hougang Avenue 3 21:34:06), exactly as POL-RD-22 uses it; it is not used to re-measure the distance.

2. Was the reroute traffic-justified? Yes (POL-RD-23). The LTA advisory EV-ADVIS-05014-01 is an ACCIDENT on the KPE towards TPE after the MacPherson Road exit, valid 21:06–22:16, overlapping the trip window (21:16–21:38), and ACCIDENT is an admitted incident type. Its road, direction and location are the judge's to match against the trip (the artifact leaves 'intersects_route' undetermined for that reason): the recommended route runs on the KPE through and past that MacPherson Road exit, and that exit is the very point the trip record gives for the deviation. The incident therefore lies on the recommended route, so the deviation was a response to real-time traffic on it. I accept the driver's claim on this and reject the rider's contrary claim that 'null' intersection means the reroute cannot be treated as justified — POL-RD-23 asks the judge to decide that from the advisory's place against the route, and it does lie on it.

3. Was the rider informed? Yes (POL-RD-21). The driver's MSG-05014-003 at 21:19:56 gave a brief reason and the intended detour, before the 21:22:26 deviation. That part of the chat log is not in issue. The driver's claim on this point is accepted.

4. Did the rider agree? This is what the case turns on, and the record cannot settle it. POL-RD-24 row (a) (no refund on a justified, over-tolerance deviation) needs the rider informed AND agreed, and POL-RD-21 says the deviation is agreed only where the chat log confirms her acknowledgment. Her only reply, MSG-05014-004 at 21:20:41 — 'aiyo can meh... ok lor whatever u say but dun charge me more ah' — mixes assent with a fare condition; the pre-pass marks EV-CHAT-05014 IMPAIRED at weight 0.85 with issue LANGUAGE_AMBIGUITY for exactly that. The log does not confirm acknowledgment, so row (a) is not made out; and a case that is informed but objected fits no row and escalates under POL-GEN-26. I therefore do not accept the driver's claim that the reply is assent to the route making the deviation agreed.

5. Confidence. The rider's profile carries a fraud flag (fraud_flags = 1), so POL-GEN-22 requires a confidence of 0.95 whatever the 4.20 SGD value. The fact that decides whether the fare stands or is refunded — whether the rider acknowledged or objected — is carried only by EV-CHAT-05014, weight 0.85. Under POL-GEN-02(2) my confidence cannot exceed the lowest weight of the artifacts carrying the deciding fact, so it is capped at 0.85, below the 0.95 bar. The rider's claim on this is accepted (the flag governs the confidence needed only; POL-GEN-01 keeps it from deciding the trip).

6. The money, for completeness. If any refund were due it would be the excess distance fare, deviation 1.30 km x base per-km rate 0.72 SGD = 0.94 SGD, without surge (POL-RD-24), and nothing has been refunded so far (payment_status CHARGED, refund_issued_sgd 0.00). Both advocates' arithmetic on this is correct, and it confirms the rider's 4.20 SGD figure is not an outcome the matrix provides even on the row most favourable to her; but no matrix row is made out on this record, so no money moves now.

Open question for the human reviewer: read MSG-05014-004 against the driver's MSG-05014-003 and decide whether the rider acknowledged the reroute (the fare stands) or objected to paying more for it (the excess distance fare of 0.94 SGD would be refunded). The chat log's ambiguity is the one fact the AI cannot resolve.

The driver-device trace corroborates both the route taken and the deviation window: 45 fixes at 30-second intervals, 100% coverage, no gaps; KPE fixes to 21:22:05, MacPherson Road from 21:22:35 to 21:28:05, Upper Paya Lebar Road to 21:34:05, rejoin at Hougang Avenue 3 at 21:34:06 - matching the trip record's route_deviation_detected at 21:22:26 and route_rejoined at 21:34:06. POL-RD-22 uses the trace for exactly this: which route was taken and when. The rider was carried off the recommended route for about twelve minutes on a route she had not agreed to pay extra for.

The only reply the driver obtained was MSG-05014-004: 'aiyo can meh... ok lor whatever u say but dun charge me more ah'. That is assent to the detour expressly conditioned on the fare, not the rider's acknowledgment of the deviation that POL-RD-21 requires, and it cannot satisfy POL-RD-24 row (a)'s 'rider informed and agreed'. The condition was sent at 21:20:41 and read by the driver at 21:21:15, before the vehicle left the KPE at 21:22:26 - so the driver read the rider's fare condition and deviated anyway.

ledger.claim: I disclose that EV-CHAT-05014 is IMPAIRED: weight_multiplier 0.85, issue code LANGUAGE_AMBIGUITY, because the one message mixes assent with a fare condition. Under POL-GEN-02 the judge's confidence on the facts that artifact carries cannot exceed 0.85, and an impaired artifact cannot be read up into a clean finding of agreement. Under POL-GEN-26, a fact the record cannot establish from impaired evidence - here, whether the rider agreed - is escalated, not resolved against the rider.

The traffic advisory (LTA-TI-260903-6975) is an ACCIDENT on the KPE towards TPE after the MacPherson Road exit, valid 21:06:05 to 22:16:05, so it overlaps the trip window. But the artifact itself records intersects_route as null and justifies_reroute as null, and states that the record does not say whether the advisory lies on the recommended route. POL-RD-23 makes intersection with the recommended route a condition of traffic justification, and that condition is left undetermined on this record. The deviation therefore cannot be taken as traffic-justified, and row (d) of POL-RD-24 applies: refund of the excess distance fare in full.

The excess distance fare under POL-RD-24 is the deviation distance times the base per-km rate, without surge: 1.30 km x 0.72 SGD = 0.94 SGD, rounded to the cent. That is the money the rider is owed, and it has not been returned: the fare breakdown shows payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.00. The policy measures the rider's recovery by the excess distance fare rather than the 4.20 SGD she asked for, and on that measure she is owed 0.94 SGD as a PARTIAL_REFUND.

On no view of this record can it end in NO_ACTION. Row (a) of POL-RD-24 is the only no-refund row available above tolerance and it needs the rider's agreement, which the conditional reply and the 0.85 impairment deny; rows (b) and (d) each return the excess distance fare. If the judge instead finds the rider was informed but cannot say whether she agreed, the case fits no row and POL-GEN-26 escalates it - and an escalated charge is held rather than borne by the rider. NO_ACTION would leave her paying for a detour she never agreed to fund.

ledger.claim: The rider's profile carries fraud_flags of 1, so under POL-GEN-22 the AI ruling on this dispute needs a confidence of 0.95 whatever the 4.20 SGD value, and POL-RD-25 requires the 1.30 km deviation to be within its 2.0 km AI limit (it is) and the confidence bar to be met. The chat that would have to carry any agreement finding is impaired at 0.85 and the advisory's intersection with the recommended route is undetermined, so if that 0.95 bar is not reached the case escalates under POL-GEN-22 rather than the rider bearing the charge. This goes to the confidence the ruling needs only; POL-GEN-01 keeps the flag from deciding the trip.

ledger.claim: The reroute was traffic-justified under POL-RD-23. EV-ADVIS-05014-01 is an LTA traffic advisory for an ACCIDENT on the Kallang-Paya Lebar Expressway (KPE) towards TPE after the MacPherson Road exit, valid 2026-09-03T21:06:05 to 22:16:05, and that window overlaps the trip window (start 21:16:05, end 21:38:05) as the trip record gives it; ACCIDENT is one of the incident types POL-RD-23 admits, and the advisory's road (KPE) and its stated location ('after MacPherson Road exit') are the road and the very point the trip record itself gives for the deviation — 'Vehicle left the recommended route at KPE / MacPherson Road exit' — on the KPE leg of the recommended route. The reroute was therefore a response to real-time traffic on the recommended route, not an unexplained detour.

The driver met POL-RD-21's notification duty. The driver's in-app message MSG-05014-003, sent at 21:19:56, reads 'Accident on KPE ahead, I exit MacPherson then go Upper Paya Lebar, can?' — a brief reason and the intended detour — and the trip record's route_deviation_detected event follows at 21:22:26, so the rider was told before the point of deviation. The chat log EV-CHAT-05014 is IMPAIRED: weight_multiplier 0.85, issue code LANGUAGE_AMBIGUITY; that impairment is recorded against the rider's reply, not against the driver's message, whose text and timestamp are not in issue.

The rider acknowledged the reroute, so the deviation is agreed and POL-RD-24(a) applies. Her reply MSG-05014-004 at 21:20:41 reads 'aiyo can meh... ok lor whatever u say but dun charge me more ah': she assents to the route ('ok lor whatever u say') and attaches her only condition to the fare, not to the route — she does not tell the driver to stay on the KPE or to turn back. POL-RD-21 provides that where the chat log confirms the rider's acknowledgment, the deviation is agreed. EV-CHAT-05014 is impaired (weight 0.85, issue LANGUAGE_AMBIGUITY) and that is disclosed here; but the very ambiguity the assessor describes — assent mixed with a fare condition — is still assent to the route, and POL-RD-24 reserves escalation for the different case of 'informed but the rider objected'.

No row of POL-RD-24 returns the 4.20 SGD the rider claims, and none can. Row (b) — the only refund row for a justified reroute — requires that the rider was not informed, and the record shows she was informed before the deviation; row (a) (informed and agreed) leaves the charge standing; and POL-RD-24's closing sentence sends an informed-but-objected case to escalation under POL-GEN-26, which orders no money at all. On any construction of the 21:20:41 message, 4.20 SGD is not an outcome the matrix provides, so the rider's claim is not supported and the present state should stand.

ledger.claim: The most the rider could be owed on this deviation is 0.94 SGD, not 4.20 SGD. POL-RD-24 fixes the excess distance fare as the deviation distance times fare_breakdown.per_km_rate_sgd, without surge; the recorded distances give 10.9 minus 9.6 = 1.30 km (POL-RD-22), and the fare ledger's own derived figures are per_km_rate_sgd 0.72 and excess_distance_fare_sgd 0.94. The ledger also shows payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.00, so nothing has been refunded and nothing more than 0.94 SGD is in play. The rider's figure of 4.20 SGD exceeds what the policy provides even on the row most favourable to her.

The deviation itself was minimal and confined to the incident segment, which fits the driver's account rather than an opportunistic detour. The GPS trace EV-GPS-05014 is COMPLETE at weight 1.0 (45 fixes at 30 s, 100% coverage, no gap over 120 s) and shows the vehicle leaving the recommended route at the KPE / MacPherson Road exit at 21:22:26, travelling on MacPherson Road and then Upper Paya Lebar Road, and rejoining the recommended route at Hougang Avenue 3 / Upper Paya Lebar Road at 21:34:06 — the route the trip record logs, with the rejoin 12 minutes after the exit. POL-RD-22 uses the trace to show which route was taken and when.

The rider's profile carries fraud_flags of 1, so POL-GEN-22 requires a confidence of 0.95 for any final AI ruling on this dispute, whatever the amount. The fact on which the rider's contrary case would turn — whether the 21:20:41 reply acknowledged or objected to the reroute — is carried only by EV-CHAT-05014 at weight 0.85, and POL-GEN-02(2) forbids a confidence above the lowest weight among the artifacts carrying the deciding fact. A refund that depends on reading that message as an objection cannot therefore be finalised by the AI; POL-GEN-22 requires the case to be escalated instead, with the fare held rather than returned.
